segments.title: What you will build
segments.body:
## What you will build

Regression and classification learned from examples that came with the right answer. **Clustering** has no answer column at all: the model looks at the data and finds groups by itself, which is why it is called unsupervised learning. K-Means does this by picking K centre points, giving every row to its nearest centre, moving each centre to the middle of its rows, and repeating until nothing changes. In this lab you will load `shoppers.csv` (45 fictional shoppers: visits per month and average spend per visit, no labels), run `KMeans` with `n_clusters=3`, print the size and the averages of each cluster, and save a scatter plot coloured by cluster to `clusters.png`. Finally you will write one sentence describing what the three groups seem to be, for example frequent small spenders and occasional big spenders.

segments.title: Lab: find three groups of shoppers

lab.title: Find three groups of shoppers with K-Means
lab.objective: Run KMeans(n_clusters=3) on visits and spend, plot the clusters in colours, save the chart and describe the groups.
lab.instructions:
The file shoppers.csv has 45 rows with two columns: visits_per_month and avg_spend (rupees per visit). There is no label column. The starter code already loads it into df.

1. Make X = df[["visits_per_month", "avg_spend"]] (both columns, in this order).
2. Create model = KMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=0, n_init=10), run labels = model.fit_predict(X) and store the result as a new column: df["cluster"] = labels.
3. Print the three cluster sizes, smallest first, and then the average of each column per cluster:
sizes = sorted(df["cluster"].value_counts().tolist())
print("Cluster sizes:", sizes)
print(df.groupby("cluster")[["visits_per_month", "avg_spend"]].mean().round(1))
4. Draw a scatter plot of visits (x) against spend (y) coloured by cluster with plt.scatter(df["visits_per_month"], df["avg_spend"], c=df["cluster"]). Add axis labels with plt.xlabel and plt.ylabel, save it with plt.savefig("clusters.png") and print:
Saved clusters.png
5. Read the averages you printed and store one sentence (at least 12 words) in description that says what each of the three groups seems to represent: how often they visit and how much they spend.

There is no screen in the lab, so do not use plt.show(); the saved file is the chart.
lab.constraints: Use KMeans from sklearn.cluster with n_clusters=3, random_state=0 and n_init=10. Keep the names df, X, model, labels, sizes and description, and the column name cluster. Save the chart as clusters.png with matplotlib; no plt.show(). No input().

lab.solution:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

df = pd.read_csv("shoppers.csv")

X = df[["visits_per_month", "avg_spend"]]

model = KMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=0, n_init=10)
labels = model.fit_predict(X)
df["cluster"] = labels

sizes = sorted(df["cluster"].value_counts().tolist())
print("Cluster sizes:", sizes)
print(df.groupby("cluster")[["visits_per_month", "avg_spend"]].mean().round(1))

plt.scatter(df["visits_per_month"], df["avg_spend"], c=df["cluster"])
plt.xlabel("Visits per month")
plt.ylabel("Average spend per visit (rupees)")
plt.title("Shopper clusters found by K-Means")
plt.savefig("clusters.png")
print("Saved clusters.png")

description = "One group visits often but spends little each time, one visits a few times a month with medium spending, and one visits rarely but spends a lot."
